text: Consider the following two statements. S1: If a candidate is known to be corrupt, then he will not be elected. S2: If a candidate is kind, he will be elected. Which one of the following statements follows from S1 and S2 as per sound inference rules of logic?
options: If a person is known to be corrupt, he is kind
If a person is not known to be corrupt, he is not kind
If a person is kind, he is not known to be corrupt
If a person is not kind, he is not known to be corrupt
solution: Write C = known to be corrupt, K = kind, E = elected. S1: C→¬E, S2: K→E. Contrapositive of S1 is E→¬C, so by hypothetical syllogism K→E→¬C, i.e. K→¬C. Equivalently, resolution on (¬C∨¬E) and (¬K∨E) gives ¬C∨¬K.
